lessons.title: Non-Fiction: The Gunpowder Plot
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about the Gunpowder Plot from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about the Gunpowder Plot.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what children know about Bonfire Night.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about the Gunpowder Plot, appropriate for the age group.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
resources_needed: Non-fiction text about the Gunpowder Plot
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about the Gunpowder Plot.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about Bonfire Night.

lessons.title: Money Recap: Coins and Notes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recognise and total UK coins and notes.
success_criteria: I can recognise coins and notes.
I can find the total value of a set of coins.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap coins and notes from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model recognising all UK coins/notes and finding totals of small collections.
lessons.independent_task: Children find the total value of given coin/note collections, e.g. money for fireworks-safe sparklers.

differentiation.support: Total collections using coins up to 50p
differentiation.greater_depth: Total collections including notes up to £20

lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline check on money recognition and totalling before the Summer term's deeper focus — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise recognising coins and notes together.

lessons.title: Why Do We Remember Bonfire Night?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why the 5th of November is remembered.
success_criteria: I can say what happened on the 5th of November 1605.
I can say why we still remember it.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss traditions on the 5th of November.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why the Gunpowder Plot is remembered as a significant historical event.
lessons.independent_task: Children record why Bonfire Night is remembered, linking to the historical event.
key_questions: Why do we still remember it centuries later?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of a significant historical event beyond living memory — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap why Bonfire Night is remembered.
lessons.home_link: Talk about Bonfire Night traditions with your family.

lessons.title: Writing About Bonfire Night Safety
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple safety instructions using imperative verbs.
success_criteria: I can write a safety instruction.
I can start with a verb (bossy word).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing safety instructions starting with an imperative verb (e.g. 'Stand back from the fire.').
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 safety instructions for Bonfire Night.
key_questions: What safety rule will you write?
Does it start with a bossy word?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note imperative sentence construction, a Year 2 grammar skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share safety instructions with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Discuss firework safety with your family.

lessons.title: Giving Change (Simple)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to work out simple change from a small purchase.
success_criteria: I can work out change from 10p.
I can explain my method.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model working out simple change from a purchase using subtraction.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve simple change problems using role-play shopping scenarios.
key_questions: How did you work it out?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record introduction to giving change, extended in Summer term — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise working out change with play or real coins.

lessons.title: Introducing Remembrance Day
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe, age-appropriately, why Remembrance Day is observed.
success_criteria: I can say when Remembrance Day is.
I can say what the poppy represents.
lessons.starter_activity: Show a poppy and ask what children know about it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss Remembrance Day sensitively and simply — remembering soldiers who served, symbolised by the poppy.
lessons.independent_task: Children create a poppy and record why we wear one, in simple, age-appropriate language.
key_questions: What does the poppy help us remember?

differentiation.support: Adult leads discussion with simple, gentle language
differentiation.greater_depth: Add a sentence about why remembering matters

lessons.assessment_notes: Note age-appropriate, sensitive engagement with a significant national event — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap why we remember on Remembrance Day.
lessons.home_link: Talk about Remembrance Day with your family.

lessons.title: Firework Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a firework picture using colour and line.
success_criteria: I can use bright colours.
I can create lines radiating outwards.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at firework pictures/photos for inspiration.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating firework effects using chalk/paint on a dark background, radiating lines.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own firework artwork.
key_questions: How will you show the lines radiating?

differentiation.greater_depth: Combine multiple firework bursts and colours

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe colour and line technique — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.home_link: Look at real or pictured fireworks with your family (safely).

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Bonfire Night Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read Bonfire-Night-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read themed words.
I can read a sentence about Bonfire Night.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to Bonfire-Night-themed words (e.g. 'fire', 'spark', 'bang').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading Bonfire Night words over the week.

lessons.title: Money Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve simple money word problems involving totals and change.
success_criteria: I can find a total cost.
I can work out change.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap totalling and change from earlier this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving money word problems using a Bonfire Night stall context (e.g. buying a toffee apple).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve money word problems, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record money problem-solving skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Make up a money word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Comparing Bonfire Night and Remembrance Day
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare two significant events in the calendar.
success_criteria: I can say what each event remembers.
I can say how they are marked differently.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap both events discussed this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing what each event commemorates and how each is marked.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a simple comparison of Bonfire Night and Remembrance Day.

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning for the comparison

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative understanding of significant calendar events — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the two events with your family.

lessons.title: Poppy Collage
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create a poppy collage using tissue paper.
success_criteria: I can layer tissue paper.
I can create a poppy shape.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at poppy pictures for inspiration.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating a poppy shape using layered red and black tissue paper.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own poppy collage.
key_questions: How will you layer your tissue paper?

differentiation.greater_depth: Add fine detail like the poppy's centre

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe collage technique applied sensitively to Remembrance — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about the poppy collage you made with your family.

lessons.title: A Minute's Reflection
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to participate respectfully in a quiet, reflective moment.
success_criteria: I can be quiet and reflective.
I can share a thought afterwards if I choose to.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss why quiet reflection is sometimes important.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a brief, calm, reflective moment linked to Remembrance, in an age-appropriate and gentle way.
lessons.independent_task: Children take part in a short, calm reflective activity (e.g. quiet listening to gentle music), then may share a thought.
key_questions: How did that quiet moment feel?
Would you like to share a thought?

differentiation.greater_depth: Share a thoughtful reflection if comfortable

lessons.assessment_notes: Note participation in a respectful, calm class activity — evidence for ENG.SL1, handled with sensitivity rather than assessed formally.
lessons.plenary: Gently recap the importance of remembering.
lessons.home_link: Share a calm moment with your family this week.

lessons.title: Number Bonds to 100 (Multiples of 10)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find number bonds to 100 using multiples of 10.
success_criteria: I can find a number bond to 100 using tens.
I can write the number sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding number bonds to 100 using multiples of ten (e.g. 30 + 70 = 100).
lessons.independent_task: Children find and record number bonds to 100 using multiples of 10.
key_questions: Can you find all the pairs?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record number bond understanding extended to 100 — evidence for MATHS.N1/N2.

lessons.title: Autumn Half-Term 2 Recap So Far
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall key facts from this half-term's history learning.
success_criteria: I can recall a fact about a significant individual.
I can recall a fact about a significant event.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the half-term's history topics (Nightingale, Seacole, Bonfire Night, Remembrance).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the half-term's history learning so far.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a quick review quiz on the half-term's history topics.
key_questions: What have we learned this half-term?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Ongoing consolidation check for the half-term's history content — evidence for HIST.1/HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate the half-term's history learning so far.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite history fact from this half-term with your family.

lessons.title: Class Remembrance Display
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to contribute art to a respectful class Remembrance display.
success_criteria: I can add my poppy to the display.
I can talk about why it matters.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap poppy collages made on Wednesday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss arranging poppies into a respectful class display.
lessons.independent_task: Children help arrange their poppy collages into a class Remembrance display.

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the display's meaning to a younger class

lessons.assessment_notes: Note respectful engagement with a sensitive class project — evidence for ART.1.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class quiet admiration of the Remembrance display.
lessons.home_link: Describe the class Remembrance display to your family.

lessons.title: Bonfire Night and Remembrance Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about this week's topics.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage covering Bonfire Night and Remembrance, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What happened in the Gunpowder Plot?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on this week's facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Money and Number Bonds
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply money and number bond skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can total and give change with money.
I can find number bonds to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of money skills and number bonds to 100.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: money, number bonds.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 11 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N1.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising money skills over the weekend.

lessons.title: Bonfire Night and Remembrance Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about these two significant events.
success_criteria: I can say why Bonfire Night is remembered.
I can say why Remembrance Day is observed.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about these significant events.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a final reflection on the week's learning.
key_questions: What have we learned this week?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning on significant national events — evidence for HIST.2.
lessons.plenary: Quiet, respectful close to the week's learning.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned this week with your family.
